change: Follow up breakouts within hours (analytics/breakouts.csv, one follow-up per run)
hypothesis: A follow-up rides a breakout's audience while it is still searching, so follow-ups lift views per Short

change: Two evergreen search Shorts a day (questions people search all year)
hypothesis: Evergreen answers keep earning search views after news fades, so the channel's daily views rise

change: Back to 24 Shorts a day (morning 12, evening 6, afternoon 6; a slot every 40 minutes)
hypothesis: More Shorts a day bring more channel views without lowering views per Short

change: A softly blurred stock video plays behind every Short (2 to 4 clips matched to the topic)
hypothesis: Movement behind the words holds more viewers past the first seconds

change: Posting round the clock (slots over all 24 hours, a day runs 07:30 to 07:30) and an upload ceiling that learns (+6 a day with no refusal)
hypothesis: The Americans and Asia watch overnight UK and a rising ceiling fills more slots, so more Shorts go out a day

change: Stop rule: a choice whose Shorts are dead a week on is never made again, and a dead Short is never followed up or remade
hypothesis: Leaving out what is dead a week on lowers the share of dead Shorts without costing volume

change: Relatable rule: every Short for the millions who know the subject; niche subjects get an ordinary angle or are skipped
hypothesis: Mass-appeal Shorts earn more views at 24 hours

change: Full-screen portrait pictures framed on faces, no picture cards; the background video only behind graphic beats
hypothesis: A full, moving first frame holds more viewers past 3 seconds

change: Writing in quality order (strongest free models first); Claude edits the title and first and last lines and writes 1 board in 4
hypothesis: Better writers make Shorts that hold viewers and earn more views

change: Each category moves to its best quarter of the day when that is 15% better (1 board in 5 keeps the first slot)
hypothesis: Posting each category when its audience watches lifts views at 24 hours

change: Fewer, better: 15 Shorts a day (volume test 24 to 30 October against 40 a day before)
hypothesis: The channel keeps 90% or more of its daily views with fewer Shorts, each one stronger

change: Category shares follow the data (drivers.csv lift squared: Music 33%, Sport 27%, Film 24%, 4% each for the rest)
hypothesis: More of the categories that win lifts views per Short; the mix must not collapse into one or two

change: Four new market categories on test (Animals, Food, Cars, History), 8% of the day each until measured
hypothesis: New markets widen the mix and find viewers the big categories miss, without weaker Shorts

change: Named series test: a recurring series and number open the title ("Song Secrets #12")
hypothesis: A recurring series gives viewers a reason to subscribe

change: The week's winning titles from other channels are shown to the writer as angles to beat, never to copy
hypothesis: Knowing what wins for everyone else lifts our titles and first lines

change: Watchlist: GTA 6, Avengers: Doomsday, Dune: Part Three and The Game Awards get places a day from build-up (2), surging (3), launch (4)
hypothesis: Being early on the big dated events catches their peaks and brings more daily views

change: Unclear narration no longer loses a Short: a third read, then a stubborn beat read again as two sentences
hypothesis: About 8% more of the day's Shorts go out, with speech viewers can follow

change: The YouTube allowance guard counts the Shorts' own uploads, and clip uploads ask it first
hypothesis: No Short fails to upload for want of allowance; clips use what is left

change: An empty model reply moves to the next model (fact packs, the writer, the clip planner)
hypothesis: Fewer runs come back with nothing, so more clips are planned and made

change: Freshness gate: a late news Short goes out only with evidence its story is alive (boards/expired, analytics/late_uploads.csv)

change: Campaigns weighed by how often our clips reach their minimum (reach share)
hypothesis: More of the day's clips go to campaigns whose minimum our clips can reach

change: A clip refused for a channel's daily limit goes to the campaign's other channels, then Quickplay Clips
hypothesis: No made clip is stranded, so more clips go up a day

change: The batch-time run works (cron fixed, waits for 19:01 UK): Instagram, Facebook and TikTok posts and campaign submissions
hypothesis: Clips are finally submitted to their campaigns, so they can earn

change: More of the day's places filled: unfilled places spill to campaigns that filled theirs, long streams planned in windows, channel ceilings fixed at 10
